title: Environmental exposures classify recorded diabetes in NHANES
summary: A learned exposure model distinguished recorded diabetes in a random NHANES holdout with AUC .78. The analysis used 8,501 participants from 2005–2016. It establishes a retrospective predictive association, with no proof that the measured chemicals cause diabetes or predict its future onset.
ai_technology: Random-forest feature screening and LASSO regression
organization: Nanjing Medical University; Nanjing University Medical School

evidence.tested: The original abstract reports 5,953 discovery and 2,548 validation participants, training-set ten-fold feature selection using RF and LASSO, and diabetes AUC .80 versus .78. Separate linear-model validation R² values were .40 for insulin, .15 for fasting glucose and .17 for two-hour glucose; these are not additional independent discovery records.
evidence.unknown: This review had the complete original abstract and metadata, not full computational Methods. Exact feature identities, endpoint definition, sampling/measurement subsets, survey weighting, missingness and detailed preprocessing containment were not authenticated. The random validation set comes from the same survey periods; no external cohort or prospective incident-diabetes prediction is established. Chemical levels can reflect correlated exposure or disease-related processes; prediction does not establish causation. A bibliographic trial label does not make this observational analysis a randomized intervention.
evidence.ai_role: Learned feature selection and penalized regression quantify the predictive association between measured environmental exposures and recorded diabetes.

source_review.scope: Complete original primary abstract, dates and institutional affiliations actually read; full-text details were not available in this bounded review.
